observation.visible_scene: A close-up, slightly high-angle view of a saucepan (blue outer wall, stainless rim, black handle projecting to the right) sitting on an electric stove burner, with a faint red glow visible at the lower left beneath the pan. The pot is filled with water at a rolling boil. A dark skillet rests on an adjacent burner in the upper-left background, against a cream-colored stovetop surface.
visible_changes: The water churns continuously throughout the excerpt: bubbles form, rise, and burst across the entire surface, with no calm interval.
Steam/haze rises above the pot and its drifting pattern changes from frame to frame.
The pot, handle, burner, and background skillet remain fixed in place; no object enters, exits, or is manipulated.
The camera shows only minor handheld jitter: the framing and the pot's position relative to the image edges shift slightly, but there is no deliberate pan, tilt, or zoom.
A small greenish fleck is intermittently visible in the water near the center, appearing and disappearing as the surface moves.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the water was just brought to a boil or had been boiling longer before this segment (the process is already underway at t=0).
Any change in heat setting, addition of ingredients, or removal of the pot after the excerpt ends.
The purpose of the boiling (nothing is added or cooked visibly within the segment).
uncertain_details: The greenish fleck cannot be confidently identified as a separate object (e.g., herb/leaf) versus a reflection or transient bubble highlight.

Tiny shifts in the pot's apparent position are most consistent with handheld camera jitter rather than the pot moving on the burner, but the background provides limited evidence to fully separate the two.
Individual bubble trajectories are hard to track frame-to-frame due to motion blur and steam, so only the overall churning is asserted.
